bull.b: AI-related demand is driving substantial current growth across semiconductor test, while compute, memory and hyperscaler adoption broaden Teradyne’s opportunity set. This supports durable revenue expansion and potential share gains as customers invest in increasingly complex devices and data-center infrastructure.

High gross and operating margins indicate a profitable business model with meaningful economics on its test platforms and related offerings. Sustained profitability provides resources for continued R&D, product development and customer support while helping Teradyne absorb normal product-mix and cycle fluctuations.

bull.t: Conservative balance sheet and cash generation
bull.b: Very low leverage limits financial strain and preserves flexibility through semiconductor cycles. Positive free cash flow and attractive returns on equity give Teradyne capacity to fund innovation, support customers, return capital and pursue strategic opportunities without relying heavily on additional borrowing.

bear.b: Teradyne’s dependence on semiconductor and electronics capital spending makes revenue sensitive to device ramps, technology transitions and customer budgets. The prior contraction demonstrates that strong growth can reverse during industry corrections, creating uncertainty around sustainable growth and resource utilization.

Memory growth can expand Teradyne’s addressable market, but lower margins in that business may dilute consolidated profitability as its mix increases. If the pressure persists into 2027, operating leverage and the conversion of strong revenue growth into earnings could remain constrained.

bear.t: Execution and timing risk from inventory and qualifications
bear.b: Building inventory ahead of demand ties up cash and raises execution risk if customer ramps or orders are delayed. Long qualification cycles also defer revenue realization, making growth timing less predictable and increasing the chance that investments temporarily outpace sales and cash generation.
